To address this challenge, we present PC-Diffuser, a safety augmentation framework that embeds a certifiable, path-consistent barrier-function structure directly into the denoising loop of diffusion planning. The key idea is to make safety an intrinsic part of trajectory generation rather than a post-hoc fix: we enforce forward invariance along the rollout while preserving the diffusion model's intended path geometry. Specifically, PC-Diffuser (i) evaluates collision risk using a capsule-distance barrier function that better reflects vehicle geometry and reduces unnecessary conservativeness, (ii) converts denoised waypoints into dynamically feasible motion under a kinematic bicycle model, and (iii) applies a path-consistent safety filter that eliminates residual constraint violations without geometric distortion, so the corrected plan remains close to the learned distribution. By injecting these safety-consistent corrections at every denoising step and feeding the refined trajectory back into the diffusion process, PC-Diffuser enables iterative, context-aware safeguarding instead of post-hoc repair...

AI.tldr: PC-Diffuser is a safety augmentation framework that embeds certifiable barrier-function structure into diffusion-based trajectory planning for autonomous driving, enabling iterative safety corrections during denoising rather than post-hoc repair.
AI.motivation: Diffusion-based trajectory planners show strong performance but are difficult to certify and can fail catastrophically in rare or out-of-distribution scenarios, creating a need for safety guarantees in data-driven autonomous driving approaches.
AI.method: PC-Diffuser embeds path-consistent barrier-function structure directly into the denoising loop, using: (i) capsule-distance barrier functions for collision risk evaluation, (ii) conversion of waypoints to dynamically feasible motion under kinematic bicycle model, and (iii) path-consistent safety filtering that eliminates constraint violations without geometric distortion.
AI.result: The framework enables iterative, context-aware safeguarding during trajectory generation, making safety an intrinsic part of the process rather than a post-hoc fix, while preserving the diffusion model's intended path geometry.
AI.conclusion: PC-Diffuser addresses the certification challenge of diffusion planners by integrating safety guarantees directly into the denoising process, creating a more robust and certifiable trajectory planning approach for autonomous driving.

title: Design of a Robot-Assisted Chemical Dialysis System
comment: Accepted at ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction (HRI'26), Late Breaking Reports 5 pages, 2 figures
summary: Scientists perform diverse manual procedures that are tedious and laborious. Such procedures are considered a bottleneck for modern experimental science, as they consume time and increase burdens in fields including material science and medicine. We employ a user-centered approach to designing a robot-assisted system for dialysis, a common multi-day purification method used in polymer and protein synthesis. Through two usability studies, we obtain participant feedback and revise design requirements to develop the final system that satisfies scientists' needs and has the potential for applications in other experimental workflows. We anticipate that integration of this system into real synthesis procedures in a chemical wet lab will decrease workload on scientists during long experimental procedures and provide an effective approach to designing more systems that have the potential to accelerate scientific discovery and liberate scientists from tedious labor.

AI.tldr: Researchers developed a robot-assisted dialysis system using user-centered design to automate tedious manual procedures in chemical wet labs, reducing scientist workload and accelerating scientific discovery.
AI.motivation: Manual experimental procedures are tedious, laborious, and time-consuming, creating bottlenecks in scientific research fields like material science and medicine. Scientists need liberation from repetitive tasks to focus on discovery.
AI.method: Employed user-centered design approach with two usability studies to gather participant feedback and revise design requirements, specifically targeting dialysis procedures in polymer and protein synthesis workflows.
AI.result: Developed a final robot-assisted dialysis system that satisfies scientists' needs and has potential for broader applications in experimental workflows beyond dialysis procedures.
AI.conclusion: Integration of such automated systems into chemical wet labs can decrease scientist workload during long procedures, accelerate scientific discovery, and provide a design template for automating other tedious experimental tasks.

title: Few-Shot Adaptation to Non-Stationary Environments via Latent Trend Embedding for Robotics
summary: Robotic systems operating in real-world environments often suffer from concept shift, where the input-output relationship changes due to latent environmental factors that are not directly observable. Conventional adaptation methods update model parameters, which may cause catastrophic forgetting and incur high computational cost. This paper proposes a latent Trend ID-based framework for few-shot adaptation in non-stationary environments. Instead of modifying model weights, a low-dimensional environmental state, referred to as the Trend ID, is estimated via backpropagation while the model parameters remain fixed. To prevent overfitting caused by per-sample latent variables, we introduce temporal regularization and a state transition model that enforces smooth evolution of the latent space. Experiments on a quantitative food grasping task demonstrate that the learned Trend IDs are distributed across distinct regions of the latent space with temporally consistent trajectories, and that few-shot adaptation to unseen environments is achieved without modifying model parameters. The proposed framework provides a scalable and interpretable solution for robotics applications operating across diverse and evolving environments.

AI.tldr: Latent Trend ID framework enables few-shot adaptation in non-stationary environments by estimating low-dimensional environmental states instead of modifying model parameters, preventing catastrophic forgetting and reducing computational cost.
AI.motivation: Robotic systems face concept shift due to latent environmental factors, and conventional adaptation methods that update model parameters cause catastrophic forgetting and high computational costs.
AI.method: Proposes a latent Trend ID framework that estimates low-dimensional environmental states (Trend IDs) via backpropagation while keeping model parameters fixed. Introduces temporal regularization and state transition model to enforce smooth latent space evolution and prevent overfitting.
AI.result: Experiments on quantitative food grasping show Trend IDs distribute across distinct latent space regions with temporally consistent trajectories. Achieves few-shot adaptation to unseen environments without modifying model parameters.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides scalable and interpretable solution for robotics operating across diverse evolving environments by adapting through latent state estimation rather than parameter updates.

title: Update-Free On-Policy Steering via Verifiers
summary: In recent years, Behavior Cloning (BC) has become one of the most prevalent methods for enabling robots to mimic human demonstrations. However, despite their successes, BC policies are often brittle and struggle with precise manipulation. To overcome these issues, we propose UF-OPS, an Update-Free On-Policy Steering method that enables the robot to predict the success likelihood of its actions and adapt its strategy at execution time. We accomplish this by training verifier functions using policy rollout data obtained during an initial evaluation of the policy. These verifiers are subsequently used to steer the base policy toward actions with a higher likelihood of success. Our method improves the performance of black-box diffusion policy, without changing the base parameters, making it light-weight and flexible. We present results from both simulation and real-world data and achieve an average 49% improvement in success rate over the base policy across 5 real tasks.

AI.tldr: UF-OPS is an update-free on-policy steering method that improves behavior cloning policies by using verifier functions to predict action success likelihood and adapt strategies at execution time without modifying base policy parameters.
AI.motivation: Behavior Cloning policies are brittle and struggle with precise manipulation despite being prevalent for robot imitation learning. There's a need to improve BC policy robustness without heavy retraining or parameter modifications.
AI.method: Train verifier functions using policy rollout data from initial policy evaluation. These verifiers predict action success likelihood and are used to steer the base policy toward higher-success actions at execution time. The approach is update-free (no parameter updates) and works with black-box diffusion policies.
AI.result: Achieves average 49% improvement in success rate over base policy across 5 real-world tasks. Method improves performance without changing base parameters, making it lightweight and flexible.
AI.conclusion: UF-OPS effectively addresses brittleness in Behavior Cloning policies by enabling on-policy steering through success prediction verifiers, providing significant performance improvements while maintaining parameter efficiency.

title: Safe Probabilistic Planning for Human-Robot Interaction using Conformal Risk Control
summary: In this paper, we present a novel probabilistic safe control framework for human-robot interaction that combines control barrier functions (CBFs) with conformal risk control to provide formal safety guarantees while considering complex human behavior. The approach uses conformal risk control to quantify and control the prediction errors in CBF safety values and establishes formal guarantees on the probability of constraint satisfaction during interaction. We introduce an algorithm that dynamically adjusts the safety margins produced by conformal risk control based on the current interaction context. Through experiments on human-robot navigation scenarios, we demonstrate that our approach significantly reduces collision rates and safety violations as compared to baseline methods while maintaining high success rates in goal-reaching tasks and efficient control. The code, simulations, and other supplementary material can be found on the project website: https://jakeagonzales.github.io/crc-cbf-website/.

AI.tldr: A probabilistic safe control framework combining control barrier functions with conformal risk control to provide formal safety guarantees for human-robot interaction while handling complex human behavior.
AI.motivation: Need for formal safety guarantees in human-robot interaction that account for complex human behavior and prediction uncertainties, while maintaining task efficiency and goal achievement.
AI.method: Combines control barrier functions (CBFs) with conformal risk control to quantify and control prediction errors in safety values, with dynamic adjustment of safety margins based on interaction context.
AI.result: Significantly reduces collision rates and safety violations compared to baseline methods while maintaining high success rates in goal-reaching tasks and efficient control in human-robot navigation scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides formal probabilistic safety guarantees for human-robot interaction, effectively balancing safety and task performance through dynamic risk-aware control adjustments.

title: SteadyTray: Learning Object Balancing Tasks in Humanoid Tray Transport via Residual Reinforcement Learning
summary: Stabilizing unsecured payloads against the inherent oscillations of dynamic bipedal locomotion remains a critical engineering bottleneck for humanoids in unstructured environments. To solve this, we introduce ReST-RL, a hierarchical reinforcement learning architecture that explicitly decouples locomotion from payload stabilization, evaluated via the SteadyTray benchmark. Rather than relying on monolithic end-to-end learning, our framework integrates a robust base locomotion policy with a dynamic residual module engineered to actively cancel gait-induced perturbations at the end-effector. This architectural separation ensures steady tray transport without degrading the underlying bipedal stability. In simulation, the residual design significantly outperforms end-to-end baselines in gait smoothness and orientation accuracy, achieving a 96.9% success rate in variable velocity tracking and 74.5% robustness against external force disturbances. Successfully deployed on the Unitree G1 humanoid hardware, this modular approach demonstrates highly reliable zero-shot sim-to-real generalization across various objects and external force disturbances.

AI.tldr: ReST-RL: Hierarchical RL framework for humanoid robots that decouples locomotion from payload stabilization, achieving robust tray transport through a residual module that cancels gait-induced perturbations.
AI.motivation: Stabilizing unsecured payloads against oscillations during bipedal locomotion is a critical bottleneck for humanoids in unstructured environments, requiring solutions that maintain both payload stability and locomotion robustness.
AI.method: Hierarchical reinforcement learning architecture with explicit decoupling: robust base locomotion policy + dynamic residual module that actively cancels gait-induced perturbations at the end-effector, evaluated via SteadyTray benchmark.
AI.result: 96.9% success rate in variable velocity tracking, 74.5% robustness against external force disturbances, significantly outperforming end-to-end baselines in gait smoothness and orientation accuracy; successfully deployed on Unitree G1 humanoid with zero-shot sim-to-real generalization.
AI.conclusion: Modular hierarchical approach effectively solves payload stabilization without degrading bipedal stability, demonstrating reliable sim-to-real transfer across various objects and disturbances.

title: FAR-Dex: Few-shot Data Augmentation and Adaptive Residual Policy Refinement for Dexterous Manipulation
comment: Accepted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026
summary: Achieving human-like dexterous manipulation through the collaboration of multi-fingered hands with robotic arms remains a longstanding challenge in robotics, primarily due to the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations and the complexity of high-dimensional action spaces. To address these challenges, we propose FAR-Dex, a hierarchical framework that integrates few-shot data augmentation with adaptive residual refinement to enable robust and precise arm-hand coordination in dexterous tasks. First, FAR-DexGen leverages the IsaacLab simulator to generate diverse and physically constrained trajectories from a few demonstrations, providing a data foundation for policy training. Second, FAR-DexRes introduces an adaptive residual module that refines policies by combining multi-step trajectory segments with observation features, thereby enhancing accuracy and robustness in manipulation scenarios. Experiments in both simulation and real-world demonstrate that FAR-Dex improves data quality by 13.4% and task success rates by 7% over state-of-the-art methods. It further achieves over 80% success in real-world tasks, enabling fine-grained dexterous manipulation with strong positional generalization.

AI.tldr: FAR-Dex: A hierarchical framework combining few-shot data augmentation and adaptive residual refinement for robust arm-hand coordination in dexterous manipulation tasks.
AI.motivation: Human-like dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands and robotic arms is challenging due to scarcity of high-quality demonstrations and complexity of high-dimensional action spaces.
AI.method: Two-stage approach: 1) FAR-DexGen uses IsaacLab simulator for few-shot data augmentation to generate diverse, physically constrained trajectories; 2) FAR-DexRes introduces adaptive residual module combining multi-step trajectory segments with observation features for policy refinement.
AI.result: Improves data quality by 13.4% and task success rates by 7% over state-of-the-art methods; achieves over 80% success in real-world tasks with strong positional generalization.
AI.conclusion: FAR-Dex enables robust and precise arm-hand coordination for fine-grained dexterous manipulation through hierarchical integration of data augmentation and adaptive refinement.

title: Recover to Predict: Progressive Retrospective Learning for Variable-Length Trajectory Prediction
summary: Trajectory prediction is critical for autonomous driving, enabling safe and efficient planning in dense, dynamic traffic. Most existing methods optimize prediction accuracy under fixed-length observations. However, real-world driving often yields variable-length, incomplete observations, posing a challenge to these methods. A common strategy is to directly map features from incomplete observations to those from complete ones. This one-shot mapping, however, struggles to learn accurate representations for short trajectories due to significant information gaps. To address this issue, we propose a Progressive Retrospective Framework (PRF), which gradually aligns features from incomplete observations with those from complete ones via a cascade of retrospective units. Each unit consists of a Retrospective Distillation Module (RDM) and a Retrospective Prediction Module (RPM), where RDM distills features and RPM recovers previous timesteps using the distilled features. Moreover, we propose a Rolling-Start Training Strategy (RSTS) that enhances data efficiency during PRF training. PRF is plug-and-play with existing methods. Extensive experiments on datasets Argoverse 2 and Argoverse 1 demonstrate the effectiveness of PRF. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouhao94/PRF.

AI.tldr: PRF is a progressive retrospective framework that gradually aligns incomplete trajectory features with complete ones using cascade units, addressing variable-length observation challenges in autonomous driving prediction.
AI.motivation: Real-world autonomous driving often encounters variable-length, incomplete trajectory observations, while existing methods are optimized for fixed-length complete observations. Direct one-shot mapping from incomplete to complete features struggles with significant information gaps in short trajectories.
AI.method: Progressive Retrospective Framework (PRF) with cascade of retrospective units (RDM for feature distillation, RPM for recovering previous timesteps), plus Rolling-Start Training Strategy (RSTS) for data efficiency. PRF is plug-and-play with existing methods.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on Argoverse 2 and Argoverse 1 datasets demonstrate PRF's effectiveness in handling variable-length incomplete observations for trajectory prediction.
AI.conclusion: PRF successfully addresses the challenge of variable-length incomplete observations in trajectory prediction through progressive feature alignment, offering a plug-and-play solution that improves upon direct one-shot mapping approaches.

title: Adaptive Manipulation Potential and Haptic Estimation for Tool-Mediated Interaction
summary: Achieving human-level dexterity in contact-rich, tool-mediated manipulation remains a significant challenge due to visual occlusion and the underdetermined nature of haptic sensing. This paper introduces a parameterized Equilibrium Manifold (EM) as a unified representation for tool-mediated interaction, and develops a closed-loop framework that integrates haptic estimation, online planning, and adaptive stiffness control. We establish a physical-geometric duality using an adaptive manipulation potential incorporating a differentiable contact model, which induces the manifold's geometric structure and ensures that complex physical interactions are encapsulated as continuous operations on the EM. Within this framework, we reformulate haptic estimation as a manifold parameter estimation problem. Specifically, a hybrid inference strategy (haptic SLAM) is employed in which discrete object shapes are classified via particle filtering, while the continuous object pose is estimated using analytical gradients for efficient optimization. By continuously updating the parameters of the manipulation potential, the framework dynamically reshapes the induced EM to guide online trajectory replanning and implement uncertainty-aware impedance control, thereby closing the perception-action loop. The system is validated through simulation and over 260 real-world screw-loosening trials. Experimental results demonstrate robust identification and manipulation success in standard scenarios while maintaining accurate tracking. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that haptic SLAM and uncertainty-aware stiffness modulation outperform fixed impedance baselines, effectively preventing jamming during tight tolerance interactions.

AI.tldr: A framework using Equilibrium Manifold representation with haptic SLAM for robust tool-mediated manipulation under visual occlusion and haptic uncertainty.
AI.motivation: Human-level dexterity in contact-rich, tool-mediated manipulation is challenging due to visual occlusion and underdetermined haptic sensing, requiring robust perception-action integration.
AI.method: Parameterized Equilibrium Manifold representation with physical-geometric duality using adaptive manipulation potential; haptic SLAM combining particle filtering for shape classification and analytical gradients for pose estimation; closed-loop integration of haptic estimation, online planning, and adaptive stiffness control.
AI.result: Validated through simulation and 260+ real-world screw-loosening trials; robust identification and manipulation success in standard scenarios with accurate tracking; haptic SLAM and uncertainty-aware stiffness modulation outperform fixed impedance baselines, preventing jamming in tight tolerance interactions.
AI.conclusion: The Equilibrium Manifold framework with haptic SLAM enables robust tool-mediated manipulation under uncertainty by unifying perception and action through geometric representation and adaptive control.

title: Interleaving Scheduling and Motion Planning with Incremental Learning of Symbolic Space-Time Motion Abstractions
summary: Task and Motion Planning combines high-level task sequencing (what to do) with low-level motion planning (how to do it) to generate feasible, collision-free execution plans. However, in many real-world domains, such as automated warehouses, tasks are predefined, shifting the challenge to if, when, and how to execute them safely and efficiently under resource, time and motion constraints. In this paper, we formalize this as the Scheduling and Motion Planning problem for multi-object navigation in shared workspaces. We propose a novel solution framework that interleaves off-the-shelf schedulers and motion planners in an incremental learning loop. The scheduler generates candidate plans, while the motion planner checks feasibility and returns symbolic feedback, i.e., spatial conflicts and timing adjustments, to guide the scheduler towards motion-feasible solutions. We validate our proposal on logistics and job-shop scheduling benchmarks augmented with motion tasks, using state-of-the-art schedulers and sampling-based motion planners. Our results show the effectiveness of our framework in generating valid plans under complex temporal and spatial constraints, where synchronized motion is critical.

AI.tldr: A framework combining scheduling and motion planning for multi-object navigation in shared workspaces, using incremental learning with feedback loops between schedulers and motion planners.
AI.motivation: In real-world domains like automated warehouses, tasks are predefined but execution must consider safety, efficiency, and feasibility under resource, time, and motion constraints, requiring integration of scheduling and motion planning.
AI.method: Proposes a novel solution framework that interleaves off-the-shelf schedulers and motion planners in an incremental learning loop, where the scheduler generates candidate plans and the motion planner checks feasibility and provides symbolic feedback (spatial conflicts, timing adjustments) to guide the scheduler.
AI.result: Validated on logistics and job-shop scheduling benchmarks augmented with motion tasks using state-of-the-art schedulers and sampling-based motion planners, showing effectiveness in generating valid plans under complex temporal and spatial constraints where synchronized motion is critical.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully addresses the Scheduling and Motion Planning problem for multi-object navigation in shared workspaces by integrating scheduling and motion planning through feedback loops, enabling generation of feasible execution plans in complex real-world scenarios.

title: Semantic Landmark Particle Filter for Robot Localisation in Vineyards
summary:
Reliable localisation in vineyards is hindered by row-level perceptual aliasing: parallel crop rows produce nearly identical LiDAR observations, causing geometry-only and vision-based SLAM systems to converge towards incorrect corridors, particularly during headland transitions. We present a Semantic Landmark Particle Filter (SLPF) that integrates trunk and pole landmark detections with 2D LiDAR within a probabilistic localisation framework. Detected trunks are converted into semantic walls, forming structural row boundaries embedded in the measurement model to improve discrimination between adjacent rows. GNSS is incorporated as a lightweight prior that stabilises localisation when semantic observations are sparse.
  Field experiments in a 10-row vineyard demonstrate consistent improvements over geometry-only (AMCL), vision-based (RTAB-Map), and GNSS baselines. Compared to AMCL, SLPF reduces Absolute Pose Error by 22% and 65% across two traversal directions; relative to a NoisyGNSS baseline, APE decreases by 65% and 61%. Row correctness improves from 0.67 to 0.73, while mean cross-track error decreases from 1.40 m to 1.26 m. These results show that embedding row-level structural semantics within the measurement model enables robust localisation in highly repetitive outdoor agricultural environments.

AI.tldr: Semantic Landmark Particle Filter (SLPF) integrates trunk/pole detections with 2D LiDAR to solve perceptual aliasing in vineyards, improving localization accuracy over geometry-only and vision-based methods.
AI.motivation: Vineyard localization is challenging due to perceptual aliasing where parallel crop rows produce nearly identical LiDAR observations, causing SLAM systems to converge to incorrect corridors during headland transitions.
AI.method: SLPF integrates trunk and pole landmark detections with 2D LiDAR within a probabilistic localization framework. Detected trunks are converted into semantic walls forming structural row boundaries embedded in the measurement model. GNSS is incorporated as a lightweight prior for stabilization when semantic observations are sparse.
AI.result: Field experiments in a 10-row vineyard show SLPF reduces Absolute Pose Error by 22% and 65% compared to AMCL, and by 65% and 61% compared to NoisyGNSS. Row correctness improves from 0.67 to 0.73, and mean cross-track error decreases from 1.40 m to 1.26 m.
AI.conclusion: Embedding row-level structural semantics within the measurement model enables robust localization in highly repetitive outdoor agricultural environments like vineyards.

title: ScanDP: Generalizable 3D Scanning with Diffusion Policy
comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Project Page: https://treeitsuki.github.io/ScanDP/
summary: Learning-based 3D Scanning plays a crucial role in enabling efficient and accurate scanning of target objects. However, recent reinforcement learning-based methods often require large-scale training data and still struggle to generalize to unseen object categories.In this work, we propose a data-efficient 3D scanning framework that uses Diffusion Policy to imitate human-like scanning strategies. To enhance robustness and generalization, we adopt the Occupancy Grid Mapping instead of direct point cloud processing, offering improved noise resilience and handling of diverse object geometries. We also introduce a hybrid approach combining a sphere-based space representation with a path optimization procedure that ensures path safety and scanning efficiency. This approach addresses limitations in conventional imitation learning, such as redundant or unpredictable behavior. We evaluate our method on diverse unseen objects in both shape and scale. Ours achieves higher coverage and shorter paths than baselines, while remaining robust to sensor noise. We further confirm practical feasibility and stable operation in real-world execution.

AI.tldr: A data-efficient 3D scanning framework using Diffusion Policy to imitate human scanning strategies, with Occupancy Grid Mapping for robustness and hybrid sphere-based representation with path optimization for safety and efficiency.
AI.motivation: Current reinforcement learning-based 3D scanning methods require large training data and struggle with generalization to unseen object categories. There's a need for more data-efficient approaches that can handle diverse geometries while maintaining robustness to sensor noise.
AI.method: 1) Uses Diffusion Policy to imitate human-like scanning strategies; 2) Adopts Occupancy Grid Mapping instead of direct point cloud processing for improved noise resilience and geometry handling; 3) Introduces hybrid approach combining sphere-based space representation with path optimization for safety and scanning efficiency; 4) Addresses limitations in conventional imitation learning like redundant/unpredictable behavior.
AI.result: Achieves higher coverage and shorter paths than baselines on diverse unseen objects in both shape and scale. Remains robust to sensor noise. Confirmed practical feasibility and stable operation in real-world execution.
AI.conclusion: The proposed data-efficient 3D scanning framework successfully addresses generalization challenges through Diffusion Policy imitation learning, Occupancy Grid Mapping for robustness, and hybrid path optimization, demonstrating practical real-world applicability.

title: GRACE: A Unified 2D Multi-Robot Path Planning Simulator & Benchmark for Grid, Roadmap, And Continuous Environments
comment: ICRA 2026, code will be released soon
summary: Advancing Multi-Agent Pathfinding (MAPF) and Multi-Robot Motion Planning (MRMP) requires platforms that enable transparent, reproducible comparisons across modeling choices. Existing tools either scale under simplifying assumptions (grids, homogeneous agents) or offer higher fidelity with less comparable instrumentation. We present GRACE, a unified 2D simulator+benchmark that instantiates the same task at multiple abstraction levels (grid, roadmap, continuous) via explicit, reproducible operators and a common evaluation protocol. Our empirical results on public maps and representative planners enable commensurate comparisons on a shared instance set. Furthermore, we quantify the expected representation-fidelity trade-offs (MRMP solves instances at higher fidelity but lower speed, while grid/roadmap planners scale farther). By consolidating representation, execution, and evaluation, GRACE thereby aims to make cross-representation studies more comparable and provides a means to advance multi-robot planning research and its translation to practice.

AI.tldr: GRACE is a unified 2D simulator+benchmark for multi-agent pathfinding that enables transparent, reproducible comparisons across different abstraction levels (grid, roadmap, continuous) with explicit operators and common evaluation protocols.
AI.motivation: Existing tools for multi-agent pathfinding and multi-robot motion planning either scale well under simplifying assumptions (grids, homogeneous agents) or offer higher fidelity but with less comparable instrumentation, creating a need for platforms that enable transparent, reproducible comparisons across different modeling choices.
AI.method: GRACE instantiates the same task at multiple abstraction levels (grid, roadmap, continuous) via explicit, reproducible operators and implements a common evaluation protocol, consolidating representation, execution, and evaluation into a unified framework.
AI.result: Empirical results on public maps with representative planners enable commensurate comparisons on a shared instance set, quantifying expected representation-fidelity trade-offs (MRMP solves instances at higher fidelity but lower speed, while grid/roadmap planners scale farther).
AI.conclusion: By providing a unified platform that consolidates representation, execution, and evaluation, GRACE aims to make cross-representation studies more comparable and provides a means to advance multi-robot planning research and its translation to practice.

title: Contact Coverage-Guided Exploration for General-Purpose Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Deep Reinforcement learning (DRL) has achieved remarkable success in domains with well-defined reward structures, such as Atari games and locomotion. In contrast, dexterous manipulation lacks general-purpose reward formulations and typically depends on task-specific, handcrafted priors to guide hand-object interactions. We propose Contact Coverage-Guided Exploration (CCGE), a general exploration method designed for general-purpose dexterous manipulation tasks. CCGE represents contact state as the intersection between object surface points and predefined hand keypoints, encouraging dexterous hands to discover diverse and novel contact patterns, namely which fingers contact which object regions. It maintains a contact counter conditioned on discretized object states obtained via learned hash codes, capturing how frequently each finger interacts with different object regions. This counter is leveraged in two complementary ways: (1) to assign a count-based contact coverage reward that promotes exploration of novel contact patterns, and (2) an energy-based reaching reward that guides the agent toward under-explored contact regions. We evaluate CCGE on a diverse set of dexterous manipulation tasks, including cluttered object singulation, constrained object retrieval, in-hand reorientation, and bimanual manipulation. Experimental results show that CCGE substantially improves training efficiency and success rates over existing exploration methods, and that the contact patterns learned with CCGE transfer robustly to real-world robotic systems. Project page is https://contact-coverage-guided-exploration.github.io.

AI.tldr: CCGE is a contact coverage-guided exploration method for dexterous manipulation that encourages discovery of diverse contact patterns between hand keypoints and object regions to improve training efficiency and success rates.
AI.motivation: Dexterous manipulation lacks general-purpose reward formulations and typically depends on task-specific, handcrafted priors, unlike domains like Atari games with well-defined reward structures. There's a need for a general exploration method for dexterous manipulation tasks.
AI.method: CCGE represents contact state as intersection between object surface points and predefined hand keypoints, maintains a contact counter conditioned on discretized object states via learned hash codes, and uses this counter for: (1) count-based contact coverage reward promoting novel contact pattern exploration, and (2) energy-based reaching reward guiding toward under-explored contact regions.
AI.result: CCGE substantially improves training efficiency and success rates over existing exploration methods on diverse dexterous manipulation tasks (cluttered object singulation, constrained object retrieval, in-hand reorientation, bimanual manipulation), and learned contact patterns transfer robustly to real-world robotic systems.
AI.conclusion: CCGE provides an effective general exploration method for dexterous manipulation that encourages discovery of diverse contact patterns, addresses the lack of general-purpose reward formulations in this domain, and enables robust transfer to real-world systems.

title: Shape Control of a Planar Hyper-Redundant Robot via Hybrid Kinematics-Informed and Learning-based Approach
summary: Hyper-redundant robots offer high dexterity, making them good at operating in confined and unstructured environments. To extend the reachable workspace, we built a multi-segment flexible rack actuated planar robot. However, the compliance of the flexible mechanism introduces instability, rendering it sensitive to external and internal uncertainties. To address these limitations, we propose a hybrid kinematics-informed and learning-based shape control method, named SpatioCoupledNet. The neural network adopts a hierarchical design that explicitly captures bidirectional spatial coupling between segments while modeling local disturbance along the robot body. A confidence-gating mechanism integrates prior kinematic knowledge, allowing the controller to adaptively balance model-based and learned components for improved convergence and fidelity. The framework is validated on a five-segment planar hyper-redundant robot under three representative shape configurations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms both analytical and purely neural controllers. In complex scenarios, it reduces steady-state error by up to 75.5% against the analytical model, and accelerates convergence by up to 20.5% compared to the data-driven baseline. Furthermore, gating analysis reveals a state-dependent authority fusion, shifting toward data-driven predictions in unstable states, while relying on physical priors in the remaining cases. Finally, we demonstrate robust performance in a dynamic task where the robot maintains a fixed end-effector position while avoiding moving obstacles, achieving a precise tip-positioning accuracy with a mean error of 10.47 mm.

AI.tldr: Hybrid kinematics-informed learning-based shape control method (SpatioCoupledNet) for multi-segment flexible planar hyper-redundant robots addresses compliance-induced instability through hierarchical neural network with bidirectional spatial coupling modeling and confidence-gating mechanism.
AI.motivation: Hyper-redundant robots offer high dexterity for confined/unstructured environments, but flexible mechanisms introduce compliance-induced instability sensitive to external/internal uncertainties, requiring robust shape control.
AI.method: Proposed SpatioCoupledNet: hybrid kinematics-informed learning-based shape control with hierarchical neural network design capturing bidirectional spatial coupling between segments and modeling local disturbances; includes confidence-gating mechanism integrating prior kinematic knowledge to adaptively balance model-based and learned components.
AI.result: Method outperforms analytical and purely neural controllers: reduces steady-state error by up to 75.5% vs analytical model, accelerates convergence by up to 20.5% vs data-driven baseline; achieves mean tip-positioning error of 10.47 mm in dynamic obstacle avoidance task; gating analysis shows state-dependent authority fusion shifting toward data-driven predictions in unstable states.
AI.conclusion: SpatioCoupledNet effectively addresses compliance-induced instability in flexible hyper-redundant robots through hybrid kinematics-learning approach with explicit spatial coupling modeling and adaptive gating, enabling robust shape control with improved accuracy and convergence in complex scenarios.

title: Rethinking Gaussian Trajectory Predictors: Calibrated Uncertainty for Safe Planning
summary: Accurate trajectory prediction is critical for safe autonomous navigation in crowded environments. While many trajectory predictors output Gaussian distributions to represent the multi-modal distribution over future pedestrian positions, the reliability of their confidence levels often remains unaddressed. This limitation can lead to unsafe or overly conservative motion planning when the predictor is integrated with an uncertainty-aware planner. Existing Gaussian trajectory predictors primarily rely on the Negative Log-Likelihood loss, which is prone to predict over- or under-confident distributions, and may compromise downstream planner safety. This paper introduces a novel loss function for calibrating prediction uncertainty which leverages Kernel Density Estimation to estimate the empirical distribution of confidence levels. The proposed formulation enforces consistency with the properties of a Gaussian assumption by explicitly matching the estimated empirical distribution to the Chi-squared distribution. To ensure accurate mean prediction, a Mean Squared Error term is also incorporated in the final loss formulation. Experimental results on real-world trajectory datasets show that our method significantly improves the reliability of confidence levels predicted by different State-Of-The-Art Gaussian trajectory predictors. We also demonstrate the importance of providing planners with reliable probabilistic insights (i.e. calibrated confidence levels) for collision-free navigation in complex scenarios. For this purpose, we integrate Gaussian trajectory predictors trained with our loss function with an uncertainty-aware Model Predictive Control on scenarios extracted from real-world datasets, achieving improved planning performance through calibrated confidence levels.

AI.tldr: Proposes a novel loss function for calibrating uncertainty in Gaussian trajectory predictors using Kernel Density Estimation and Chi-squared distribution matching to improve confidence reliability for safer autonomous navigation.
AI.motivation: Existing Gaussian trajectory predictors often produce unreliable confidence levels (over- or under-confident distributions) due to reliance on Negative Log-Likelihood loss, which compromises safety when integrated with uncertainty-aware motion planners in crowded environments.
AI.method: Introduces a calibration loss function that uses Kernel Density Estimation to estimate empirical distribution of confidence levels and enforces consistency with Gaussian assumptions by matching to Chi-squared distribution. Incorporates Mean Squared Error term for accurate mean prediction.
AI.result: Experimental results on real-world trajectory datasets show significant improvement in confidence level reliability for various State-Of-The-Art Gaussian trajectory predictors. Integration with uncertainty-aware Model Predictive Control demonstrates improved planning performance and collision-free navigation in complex scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The proposed calibration method effectively addresses reliability issues in Gaussian trajectory predictors, providing planners with calibrated confidence levels that enhance safety and performance in autonomous navigation systems.

title: COHORT: Hybrid RL for Collaborative Large DNN Inference on Multi-Robot Systems Under Real-Time Constraints
comment: Recently accepted at 27th IEEE International Symposium on a World of Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks ( IEEE WoWMoM 2026)
summary: Large deep neural networks (DNNs), especially transformer-based and multimodal architectures, are computationally demanding and challenging to deploy on resource-constrained edge platforms like field robots. These challenges intensify in mission-critical scenarios (e.g., disaster response), where robots must collaborate under tight constraints on bandwidth, latency, and battery life, often without infrastructure or server support. To address these limitations, we present COHORT, a collaborative DNN inference and task-execution framework for multi-robot systems built on the Robotic Operating System (ROS). COHORT employs a hybrid offline-online reinforcement learning (RL) strategy to dynamically schedule and distribute DNN module execution across robots. Our key contributions are threefold: (a) Offline RL policy learning combined with Advantage-Weighted Regression (AWR), trained on auction-based task allocation data from heterogeneous DNN workloads across distributed robots, (b) Online policy adaptation via Multi-Agent PPO (MAPPO), initialized from the offline policy and fine-tuned in real time, and (c) comprehensive evaluation of COHORT on vision-language model (VLM) inference tasks such as CLIP and SAM, analyzing scalability with increasing robot/workload and robustness under . We benchmark COHORT against genetic algorithms and multiple RL baselines. Experimental results demonstrate that COHORT reduces battery consumption by 15.4% and increases GPU utilization by 51.67%, while satisfying frame-rate and deadline constraints 2.55 times of the time.

AI.tldr: COHORT is a collaborative DNN inference framework for multi-robot systems that uses hybrid offline-online RL to dynamically schedule and distribute DNN module execution across robots, reducing battery consumption by 15.4% and increasing GPU utilization by 51.67% while meeting performance constraints.
AI.motivation: Large DNNs, especially transformer-based and multimodal architectures, are computationally demanding and challenging to deploy on resource-constrained edge platforms like field robots. These challenges intensify in mission-critical scenarios where robots must collaborate under tight constraints on bandwidth, latency, and battery life without infrastructure or server support.
AI.method: COHORT employs a hybrid offline-online RL strategy: (a) Offline RL policy learning with Advantage-Weighted Regression (AWR) trained on auction-based task allocation data from heterogeneous DNN workloads, (b) Online policy adaptation via Multi-Agent PPO (MAPPO) initialized from the offline policy and fine-tuned in real time, built on ROS for multi-robot systems.
AI.result: COHORT reduces battery consumption by 15.4% and increases GPU utilization by 51.67%, while satisfying frame-rate and deadline constraints 2.55 times of the time. It was benchmarked against genetic algorithms and multiple RL baselines on VLM inference tasks (CLIP and SAM).
AI.conclusion: COHORT effectively addresses the computational challenges of deploying large DNNs on resource-constrained multi-robot systems through collaborative inference and dynamic scheduling, demonstrating significant improvements in energy efficiency and computational resource utilization while maintaining performance constraints.

title: AsyncMDE: Real-Time Monocular Depth Estimation via Asynchronous Spatial Memory
summary: Foundation-model-based monocular depth estimation offers a viable alternative to active sensors for robot perception, yet its computational cost often prohibits deployment on edge platforms. Existing methods perform independent per-frame inference, wasting the substantial computational redundancy between adjacent viewpoints in continuous robot operation. This paper presents AsyncMDE, an asynchronous depth perception system consisting of a foundation model and a lightweight model that amortizes the foundation model's computational cost over time. The foundation model produces high-quality spatial features in the background, while the lightweight model runs asynchronously in the foreground, fusing cached memory with current observations through complementary fusion, outputting depth estimates, and autoregressively updating the memory. This enables cross-frame feature reuse with bounded accuracy degradation. At a mere 3.83M parameters, it operates at 237 FPS on an RTX 4090, recovering 77% of the accuracy gap to the foundation model while achieving a 25X parameter reduction. Validated across indoor static, dynamic, and synthetic extreme-motion benchmarks, AsyncMDE degrades gracefully between refreshes and achieves 161FPS on a Jetson AGX Orin with TensorRT, clearly demonstrating its feasibility for real-time edge deployment.

AI.tldr: AsyncMDE is an asynchronous depth perception system that combines a foundation model for high-quality features with a lightweight model for real-time inference, enabling efficient cross-frame feature reuse for edge deployment.
AI.motivation: Foundation-model-based monocular depth estimation is computationally expensive for edge platforms, and existing methods waste computational redundancy between adjacent frames in continuous robot operation by performing independent per-frame inference.
AI.method: AsyncMDE uses a two-model asynchronous system: a foundation model produces high-quality spatial features in the background, while a lightweight model (3.83M parameters) runs asynchronously in the foreground, fusing cached memory with current observations through complementary fusion, outputting depth estimates, and autoregressively updating memory for cross-frame feature reuse.
AI.result: The system achieves 237 FPS on RTX 4090, recovers 77% of the accuracy gap to the foundation model while achieving 25X parameter reduction, and maintains 161 FPS on Jetson AGX Orin with TensorRT. It demonstrates graceful degradation between refreshes across indoor static, dynamic, and synthetic extreme-motion benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: AsyncMDE enables efficient real-time edge deployment of foundation-model-based depth estimation by amortizing computational costs over time through asynchronous operation and cross-frame feature reuse, making it feasible for robot perception applications.

title: KnowDiffuser: A Knowledge-Guided Diffusion Planner with LM Reasoning and Prior-Informed Trajectory Initialization
summary: Recent advancements in Language Models (LMs) have demonstrated strong semantic reasoning capabilities, enabling their application in high-level decision-making for autonomous driving (AD). However, LMs operate over discrete token spaces and lack the ability to generate continuous, physically feasible trajectories required for motion planning. Meanwhile, diffusion models have proven effective at generating reliable and dynamically consistent trajectories, but often lack semantic interpretability and alignment with scene-level understanding. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{KnowDiffuser}, a knowledge-guided motion planning framework that tightly integrates the semantic understanding of language models with the generative power of diffusion models. The framework employs a language model to infer context-aware meta-actions from structured scene representations, which are then mapped to prior trajectories that anchor the subsequent denoising process. A two-stage truncated denoising mechanism refines these trajectories efficiently, preserving both semantic alignment and physical feasibility. Experiments on the nuPlan benchmark demonstrate that KnowDiffuser significantly outperforms existing planners in both open-loop and closed-loop evaluations, establishing a robust and interpretable framework that effectively bridges the semantic-to-physical gap in AD systems.

AI.tldr: KnowDiffuser integrates language models' semantic reasoning with diffusion models' trajectory generation for autonomous driving motion planning, achieving state-of-the-art performance on nuPlan benchmark.
AI.motivation: Language models have strong semantic reasoning but can't generate continuous trajectories, while diffusion models produce physically feasible trajectories but lack semantic interpretability and scene-level understanding. There's a need to bridge this semantic-to-physical gap in autonomous driving systems.
AI.method: A knowledge-guided motion planning framework that uses language models to infer context-aware meta-actions from structured scene representations, maps these to prior trajectories, and employs a two-stage truncated denoising mechanism to refine trajectories while preserving semantic alignment and physical feasibility.
AI.result: KnowDiffuser significantly outperforms existing planners in both open-loop and closed-loop evaluations on the nuPlan benchmark, establishing robust and interpretable performance.
AI.conclusion: The framework effectively bridges the semantic-to-physical gap in autonomous driving systems by tightly integrating language models' semantic understanding with diffusion models' generative capabilities for motion planning.

title: DiT4DiT: Jointly Modeling Video Dynamics and Actions for Generalizable Robot Control
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot learning, but their representations are still largely inherited from static image-text pretraining, leaving physical dynamics to be learned from comparatively limited action data. Generative video models, by contrast, encode rich spatiotemporal structure and implicit physics, making them a compelling foundation for robotic manipulation. But their potentials are not fully explored in the literature. To bridge the gap, we introduce DiT4DiT, an end-to-end Video-Action Model that couples a video Diffusion Transformer with an action Diffusion Transformer in a unified cascaded framework. Instead of relying on reconstructed future frames, DiT4DiT extracts intermediate denoising features from the video generation process and uses them as temporally grounded conditions for action prediction. We further propose a dual flow-matching objective with decoupled timesteps and noise scales for video prediction, hidden-state extraction, and action inference, enabling coherent joint training of both modules. Across simulation and real-world benchmarks, DiT4DiT achieves state-of-the-art results, reaching average success rates of 98.6% on LIBERO and 50.8% on RoboCasa GR1 while using substantially less training data. On the Unitree G1 robot, it also delivers superior real-world performance and strong zero-shot generalization. Importantly, DiT4DiT improves sample efficiency by over 10x and speeds up convergence by up to 7x, demonstrating that video generation can serve as an effective scaling proxy for robot policy learning. We release code and models at https://dit4dit.github.io/.

AI.tldr: DiT4DiT is a Video-Action Model that couples video and action Diffusion Transformers in a unified cascaded framework, using intermediate denoising features from video generation as temporally grounded conditions for action prediction, achieving state-of-the-art robotic manipulation performance with superior sample efficiency.
AI.motivation: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit representations from static image-text pretraining, requiring physical dynamics to be learned from limited action data. Generative video models encode rich spatiotemporal structure and implicit physics, but their potential for robotic manipulation remains underexplored.
AI.method: DiT4DiT couples a video Diffusion Transformer with an action Diffusion Transformer in a unified cascaded framework. It extracts intermediate denoising features from video generation as temporally grounded conditions for action prediction, and uses a dual flow-matching objective with decoupled timesteps and noise scales for joint training.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art results: 98.6% average success on LIBERO and 50.8% on RoboCasa GR1 with substantially less training data. On Unitree G1 robot, delivers superior real-world performance and strong zero-shot generalization. Improves sample efficiency by over 10x and speeds up convergence by up to 7x.
AI.conclusion: Video generation can serve as an effective scaling proxy for robot policy learning, bridging the gap between generative video models and robotic manipulation. The unified Video-Action Model demonstrates superior performance, sample efficiency, and generalization capabilities.

title: DepthCache: Depth-Guided Training-Free Visual Token Merging for Vision-Language-Action Model Inference
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable generalist robotic manipulation but suffer from high inference latency. This bottleneck stems from the massive number of visual tokens processed by large language backbones. Existing methods either prune or merge tokens uniformly, degrading the spatial reasoning essential for robotic control. We present DepthCache, a training-free framework that leverages depth as a structural prior for visual token compression. It partitions observations into depth-based regions and applies spatially differentiated merge ratios, preserving the near-field workspace while compressing the distant background. To exploit temporal redundancy, DepthCache distributes the merging process across consecutive frames, ensuring consistent representations while reducing per-step computation. A motion-adaptive pipeline further optimizes auxiliary view compression based on end-effector dynamics. The framework requires no model modification, generalizing across diverse VLA architectures. On the LIBERO benchmark, DepthCache achieves up to 1.28x inference speedup with less than 1% average success rate degradation across three VLA models (pi_0.5, OpenVLA, GR00T), whereas pruning and merging baselines incur 4--24% degradation at comparable compression. Real-world experiments on a physical manipulator demonstrate that DepthCache enables faster task throughput and more responsive closed-loop control in latency-sensitive scenarios.

AI.tldr: DepthCache: Training-free framework using depth-based visual token compression for Vision-Language-Action models, achieving 1.28x speedup with minimal performance degradation.
AI.motivation: VLA models suffer from high inference latency due to processing massive visual tokens, and existing uniform token pruning/merging methods degrade spatial reasoning essential for robotic control.
AI.method: Leverages depth as structural prior for visual token compression: partitions observations into depth-based regions with spatially differentiated merge ratios (preserve near-field, compress distant background). Distributes merging across consecutive frames to exploit temporal redundancy. Includes motion-adaptive pipeline for auxiliary view compression based on end-effector dynamics. Requires no model modification.
AI.result: On LIBERO benchmark: up to 1.28x inference speedup with <1% average success rate degradation across three VLA models (pi_0.5, OpenVLA, GR00T). Baselines incur 4-24% degradation at comparable compression. Real-world experiments show faster task throughput and more responsive closed-loop control.
AI.conclusion: DepthCache effectively reduces VLA inference latency while preserving spatial reasoning through depth-aware token compression, enabling faster robotic control without model modifications.

title: BinWalker: Development and Field Evaluation of a Quadruped Manipulator Platform for Sustainable Litter Collection
summary: Litter pollution represents a growing environmental problem affecting natural and urban ecosystems worldwide. Waste discarded in public spaces often accumulates in areas that are difficult to access, such as uneven terrains, coastal environments, parks, and roadside vegetation. Over time, these materials degrade and release harmful substances, including toxic chemicals and microplastics, which can contaminate soil and water and pose serious threats to wildlife and human health. Despite increasing awareness of the problem, litter collection is still largely performed manually by human operators, making large-scale cleanup operations labor-intensive, time-consuming, and costly. Robotic solutions have the potential to support and partially automate environmental cleanup tasks. In this work, we present a quadruped robotic system designed for autonomous litter collection in challenging outdoor scenarios. The robot combines the mobility advantages of legged locomotion with a manipulation system consisting of a robotic arm and an onboard litter container. This configuration enables the robot to detect, grasp, and store litter items while navigating through uneven terrains. The proposed system aims to demonstrate the feasibility of integrating perception, locomotion, and manipulation on a legged robotic platform for environmental cleanup tasks. Experimental evaluations conducted in outdoor scenarios highlight the effectiveness of the approach and its potential for assisting large-scale litter removal operations in environments that are difficult to reach with traditional robotic platforms. The code associated with this work can be found at: https://github.com/iit-DLSLab/trash-collection-isaaclab.

AI.tldr: A quadruped robot system for autonomous litter collection in challenging outdoor environments, combining legged locomotion with robotic arm manipulation for detecting, grasping, and storing litter in difficult-to-access areas.
AI.motivation: Litter pollution is a growing environmental problem affecting ecosystems worldwide, with waste accumulating in difficult-to-access areas like uneven terrains, coastal environments, and roadside vegetation. Current manual cleanup operations are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and costly, creating a need for robotic solutions to support and automate environmental cleanup tasks.
AI.method: The paper presents a quadruped robotic system that combines the mobility advantages of legged locomotion with a manipulation system consisting of a robotic arm and onboard litter container. The system integrates perception, locomotion, and manipulation capabilities to enable autonomous detection, grasping, and storage of litter items while navigating through challenging outdoor terrains.
AI.result: Experimental evaluations in outdoor scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach, showing the system's potential for assisting large-scale litter removal operations in environments that are difficult to reach with traditional robotic platforms.
AI.conclusion: The work successfully demonstrates the feasibility of integrating perception, locomotion, and manipulation on a legged robotic platform for environmental cleanup tasks, offering a promising solution for automating litter collection in challenging outdoor scenarios that are inaccessible to conventional robotic systems.

title: TacLoc: Global Tactile Localization on Objects from a Registration Perspective
summary: Pose estimation is essential for robotic manipulation, particularly when visual perception is occluded during gripper-object interactions. Existing tactile-based methods generally rely on tactile simulation or pre-trained models, which limits their generalizability and efficiency. In this study, we propose TacLoc, a novel tactile localization framework that formulates the problem as a one-shot point cloud registration task. TacLoc introduces a graph-theoretic partial-to-full registration method, leveraging dense point clouds and surface normals from tactile sensing for efficient and accurate pose estimation. Without requiring rendered data or pre-trained models, TacLoc achieves improved performance through normal-guided graph pruning and a hypothesis-and-verification pipeline. TacLoc is evaluated extensively on the YCB dataset. We further demonstrate TacLoc on real-world objects across two different visual-tactile sensors.

AI.tldr: TacLoc is a tactile localization framework that formulates pose estimation as one-shot point cloud registration, using graph-theoretic partial-to-full registration with tactile point clouds and normals, achieving improved performance without rendered data or pre-trained models.
AI.motivation: Pose estimation is crucial for robotic manipulation, especially when visual perception is occluded during gripper-object interactions. Existing tactile-based methods rely on tactile simulation or pre-trained models, limiting generalizability and efficiency.
AI.method: TacLoc formulates tactile localization as a one-shot point cloud registration task. It introduces a graph-theoretic partial-to-full registration method using dense point clouds and surface normals from tactile sensing. The approach employs normal-guided graph pruning and a hypothesis-and-verification pipeline without requiring rendered data or pre-trained models.
AI.result: TacLoc is extensively evaluated on the YCB dataset and demonstrates improved performance. It is further validated on real-world objects across two different visual-tactile sensors.
AI.conclusion: TacLoc provides an efficient and accurate tactile localization framework that addresses limitations of existing methods by eliminating the need for rendered data or pre-trained models, demonstrating practical applicability on real-world objects with different sensor types.

title: Safety-critical Control Under Partial Observability: Reach-Avoid POMDP meets Belief Space Control
summary: Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) provide a principled framework for robot decision-making under uncertainty. Solving reach-avoid POMDPs, however, requires coordinating three distinct behaviors: goal reaching, safety, and active information gathering to reduce uncertainty. Existing online POMDP solvers attempt to address all three within a single belief tree search, but this unified approach struggles with the conflicting time scales inherent to these objectives. We propose a layered, certificate-based control architecture that operates directly in belief space, decoupling goal reaching, information gathering, and safety into modular components. We introduce Belief Control Lyapunov Functions (BCLFs) that formalize information gathering as a Lyapunov convergence problem in belief space, and show how they can be learned via reinforcement learning. For safety, we develop Belief Control Barrier Functions (BCBFs) that leverage conformal prediction to provide probabilistic safety guarantees over finite horizons. The resulting control synthesis reduces to lightweight quadratic programs solvable in real time, even for non-Gaussian belief representations with dimension $>10^4$. Experiments in simulation and on a space-robotics platform demonstrate real-time performance and improved safety and task success compared to state-of-the-art constrained POMDP solvers.

AI.tldr: Layered control architecture for POMDPs decouples goal reaching, information gathering, and safety using belief-space Lyapunov and barrier functions with real-time quadratic programming.
AI.motivation: Existing online POMDP solvers struggle with coordinating conflicting time scales of goal reaching, safety, and information gathering in reach-avoid problems within a single belief tree search.
AI.method: Proposed layered certificate-based control architecture with Belief Control Lyapunov Functions (BCLFs) for information gathering learned via RL, and Belief Control Barrier Functions (BCBFs) using conformal prediction for probabilistic safety guarantees, reduced to real-time quadratic programs.
AI.result: Real-time performance with lightweight quadratic programs solvable for non-Gaussian beliefs with dimension >10^4, improved safety and task success compared to state-of-the-art constrained POMDP solvers in simulation and space-robotics platform.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling POMDP objectives into modular components with certificate-based control enables real-time performance with formal guarantees, addressing limitations of unified belief tree search approaches.

title: Learning Bimanual Cloth Manipulation with Vision-based Tactile Sensing via Single Robotic Arm
summary: Robotic cloth manipulation remains challenging due to the high-dimensional state space of fabrics, their deformable nature, and frequent occlusions that limit vision-based sensing. Although dual-arm systems can mitigate some of these issues, they increase hardware and control complexity. This paper presents Touch G.O.G., a compact vision-based tactile gripper and perception/control framework for single-arm bimanual cloth manipulation. The proposed framework combines three key components: (1) a novel gripper design and control strategy for in-gripper cloth sliding with a single robot arm, (2) a Vision Foundation Model-backboned Vision Transformer pipeline for cloth part classification (PC-Net) and edge pose estimation (PE-Net) using real and synthetic tactile images, and (3) an encoder-decoder synthetic data generator (SD-Net) that reduces manual annotation by producing high-fidelity tactile images. Experiments show 96% accuracy in distinguishing edges, corners, interior regions, and grasp failures, together with sub-millimeter edge localization and 4.5° orientation error. Real-world results demonstrate reliable cloth unfolding, even for crumpled fabrics, using only a single robotic arm. These results highlight Touch G.O.G. as a compact and cost-effective solution for deformable object manipulation.

AI.tldr: Touch G.O.G. is a vision-based tactile gripper system for single-arm bimanual cloth manipulation using tactile sensing, foundation models, and synthetic data generation to overcome challenges in deformable object manipulation.
AI.motivation: Robotic cloth manipulation is challenging due to fabrics' high-dimensional state space, deformable nature, and vision occlusions. Dual-arm systems help but increase complexity. There's a need for compact, single-arm solutions with effective tactile sensing.
AI.method: 1) Novel gripper design and control for in-gripper cloth sliding with single robot arm; 2) Vision Foundation Model-backboned Vision Transformer pipeline for cloth part classification (PC-Net) and edge pose estimation (PE-Net) using real/synthetic tactile images; 3) Encoder-decoder synthetic data generator (SD-Net) to reduce manual annotation.
AI.result: 96% accuracy in distinguishing edges, corners, interior regions, and grasp failures; sub-millimeter edge localization; 4.5° orientation error. Real-world demonstrations show reliable cloth unfolding, even for crumpled fabrics, using only a single robotic arm.
AI.conclusion: Touch G.O.G. provides a compact, cost-effective solution for deformable object manipulation, demonstrating that single-arm systems with advanced tactile perception can achieve reliable cloth manipulation comparable to more complex dual-arm setups.

title: AdaClearGrasp: Learning Adaptive Clearing for Zero-Shot Robust Dexterous Grasping in Densely Cluttered Environments
summary: In densely cluttered environments, physical interference, visual occlusions, and unstable contacts often cause direct dexterous grasping to fail, while aggressive singulation strategies may compromise safety. Enabling robots to adaptively decide whether to clear surrounding objects or directly grasp the target is therefore crucial for robust manipulation. We propose AdaClearGrasp, a closed-loop decision-execution framework for adaptive clearing and zero-shot dexterous grasping in densely cluttered environments. The framework formulates manipulation as a controllable high-level decision process that determines whether to directly grasp the target or first clear surrounding objects. A pretrained vision-language model (VLM) interprets visual observations and language task descriptions to reason about grasp interference and generate a high-level planning skeleton, which invokes structured atomic skills through a unified action interface. For dexterous grasping, we train a reinforcement learning policy with a relative hand-object distance representation, enabling zero-shot generalization across diverse object geometries and physical properties. During execution, visual feedback monitors outcomes and triggers replanning upon failures, forming a closed-loop correction mechanism. To evaluate language-conditioned dexterous grasping in clutter, we introduce Clutter-Bench, the first simulation benchmark with graded clutter complexity. It includes seven target objects across three clutter levels, yielding 210 task scenarios. We further perform sim-to-real experiments on three objects under three clutter levels (18 scenarios). Results demonstrate that AdaClearGrasp significantly improves grasp success rates in densely cluttered environments. For more videos and code, please visit our project website: https://chenzixuan99.github.io/adaclear-grasp.github.io/.

AI.tldr: AdaClearGrasp is a closed-loop framework that adaptively decides between clearing surrounding objects or directly grasping targets in dense clutter using vision-language reasoning and zero-shot dexterous grasping.
AI.motivation: In densely cluttered environments, direct dexterous grasping often fails due to physical interference, visual occlusions, and unstable contacts, while aggressive singulation strategies may compromise safety. There's a need for robots to adaptively decide whether to clear surrounding objects or directly grasp targets for robust manipulation.
AI.method: A closed-loop decision-execution framework with: 1) A pretrained vision-language model (VLM) that interprets visual observations and language task descriptions to reason about grasp interference and generate high-level planning skeletons; 2) Structured atomic skills invoked through a unified action interface; 3) A reinforcement learning policy for dexterous grasping with relative hand-object distance representation enabling zero-shot generalization; 4) Visual feedback monitoring and replanning triggered upon failures.
AI.result: The framework was evaluated on Clutter-Bench, the first simulation benchmark with graded clutter complexity (7 target objects across 3 clutter levels, 210 task scenarios). Sim-to-real experiments on 3 objects under 3 clutter levels (18 scenarios) demonstrated that AdaClearGrasp significantly improves grasp success rates in densely cluttered environments.
AI.conclusion: AdaClearGrasp provides an effective solution for adaptive clearing and zero-shot dexterous grasping in densely cluttered environments by combining vision-language reasoning with closed-loop decision-making, addressing the fundamental challenge of when to clear versus when to grasp directly.

title: STM32-Based Smart Waste Bin for Hygienic Disposal Using Embedded Sensing and Automated Control
comment: This paper consists of 6 pages, with 3 figures, 3 tables, and 1 algorithm
summary: The increasing demand for hygienic and contactless solutions in public and private environments has encouraged the development of automated systems for everyday applications. This paper presents the design and implementation of a motion- sensing automatic waste bin using an STM32 microcontroller, ultrasonic sensors, and a servo motor. The system detects user presence through ultrasonic sensing and automatically opens the bin lid using a servo motor controlled by the microcontroller. An additional ultrasonic sensor is used to monitor the internal waste level of the bin, while an OLED display provides real- time feedback regarding system status. The proposed system offers a low-cost, reliable, and easily deployable solution for touch-free waste disposal. Experimental evaluation demonstrates fast response time, stable sensing performance, and smooth mechanical operation. The system can be effectively deployed in homes, educational institutions, hospitals, and public facilities to improve hygiene and user convenience.

AI.tldr: Design and implementation of a motion-sensing automatic waste bin using STM32 microcontroller, ultrasonic sensors, and servo motor for contactless waste disposal.
AI.motivation: Increasing demand for hygienic and contactless solutions in public and private environments due to hygiene concerns and convenience needs.
AI.method: Uses STM32 microcontroller with ultrasonic sensors for user presence detection and waste level monitoring, servo motor for automatic lid opening, and OLED display for real-time status feedback.
AI.result: Experimental evaluation shows fast response time, stable sensing performance, smooth mechanical operation, and reliable touch-free waste disposal functionality.
AI.conclusion: The system provides a low-cost, reliable, and easily deployable solution for touch-free waste disposal suitable for homes, educational institutions, hospitals, and public facilities.

title: Dynamic Modeling and Attitude Control of a Reaction-Wheel-Based Low-Gravity Bipedal Hopper
summary: Planetary bodies characterized by low gravitational acceleration, such as the Moon and near-Earth asteroids, impose unique locomotion constraints due to diminished contact forces and extended airborne intervals. Among traversal strategies, hopping locomotion offers high energy efficiency but is prone to mid-flight attitude instability caused by asymmetric thrust generation and uneven terrain interactions. This paper presents an underactuated bipedal hopping robot that employs an internal reaction wheel to regulate body posture during the ballistic flight phase. The system is modeled as a gyrostat, enabling analysis of the dynamic coupling between torso rotation and reaction wheel momentum. The locomotion cycle comprises three phases: a leg-driven propulsive jump, mid-air attitude stabilization via an active momentum exchange controller, and a shock-absorbing landing. A reduced-order model is developed to capture the critical coupling between torso rotation and reaction wheel dynamics. The proposed framework is evaluated in MuJoCo-based simulations under lunar gravity conditions (g = 1.625 m/s^2). Results demonstrate that activation of the reaction wheel controller reduces peak mid-air angular deviation by more than 65% and constrains landing attitude error to within 3.5 degrees at touchdown. Additionally, actuator saturation per hop cycle is reduced, ensuring sufficient control authority. Overall, the approach significantly mitigates in-flight attitude excursions and enables consistent upright landings, providing a practical and control-efficient solution for locomotion on irregular extraterrestrial terrains.

AI.tldr: An underactuated bipedal hopping robot uses an internal reaction wheel for mid-flight attitude stabilization in low-gravity environments like the Moon, reducing angular deviation by 65% and landing error to within 3.5 degrees.
AI.motivation: Low-gravity planetary bodies (Moon, asteroids) present locomotion challenges with diminished contact forces and extended airborne phases. Hopping locomotion is energy-efficient but suffers from mid-flight attitude instability due to asymmetric thrust and uneven terrain interactions.
AI.method: An underactuated bipedal hopping robot with internal reaction wheel for attitude regulation during ballistic flight. System modeled as a gyrostat to analyze dynamic coupling between torso rotation and reaction wheel momentum. Three-phase locomotion cycle: leg-driven propulsive jump, mid-air attitude stabilization via active momentum exchange controller, and shock-absorbing landing. Reduced-order model captures critical coupling dynamics.
AI.result: MuJoCo simulations under lunar gravity (g = 1.625 m/s²) show reaction wheel controller reduces peak mid-air angular deviation by >65% and constrains landing attitude error to within 3.5 degrees. Actuator saturation per hop cycle is reduced, ensuring sufficient control authority.
AI.conclusion: The approach significantly mitigates in-flight attitude excursions and enables consistent upright landings, providing a practical and control-efficient solution for locomotion on irregular extraterrestrial terrains.

title: OnFly: Onboard Zero-Shot Aerial Vision-Language Navigation toward Safety and Efficiency
summary: Aerial vision-language navigation (AVLN) enables UAVs to follow natural-language instructions in complex 3D environments.
